narr: A period of persistent thunderstorms moved through the area with an initial warm front early in the morning and later a weak cold front overnight. Weak instability resulted in mostly benign activity, aside from a single report of each hail and wind damage. Rainfall amounts of 2.5 to 5 inches stretched across central Georgia, with highest amounts along the Georgia-Alabama line, between LaGrange and Columbus. Isolated flash flooding resulted from the heavy rainfall amounts.
ev: The broadcast media reported at least one foot of flowing water from Lindsey Creek covering both lanes of Effingham Way near Effingham Court. Radar estimates indicate 6 to 8 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Department of Transportation reported all lanes on Manchester Expressway was closed for an hour due to flooding of the highway. Radar estimates indicate 6 to 8 inches of rain fell quickly over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Department of Transportation reported I-185 Southbound closed near Exit 7 due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate 6 to 8 inches of rain fell quickly over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Bankston Road, north of Vega Road, was closed due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported Campbell Road closed due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Old Zebulon Road was closed due to high water on Powder Creek. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Turner Road, between Concord Road and Milner Road, closed due to flooding of Birch Creek. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Hunter Road closed due to high flows on Elkins Creek and a smaller tributary. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Scott Road closed due to flooding from high water on a nearby creek. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Bethany Church Road, between Dunbar School Road and Jonathans Roost Road, due to high water on local creeks. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Lipham Road flooded at two points, including at Brush Creek where a small bridge along the gravel road was washed out due to the high flow. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 5 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the roadway flooded at the Hilly Mill Creek culvert, near the intersection of George Brown Road and Joe Stephens Road. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 5 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Dallas Mill Road flooded due to high flow on Big Springs Creek. Radar estimates indicate 4 to 6 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The public relayed a report of flood waters from a nearby creek overwhelming a culvert, resulting in the evacuation of twelve homes on Valley Hill Road. No homes were flooded. Radar estimates indicate 3 to 4 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported multiple roads closed due to flash flooding including: James Posey Road, Ellison Pound Road, Howard Road, and Carlisle Road. Ellison Road remained closed after the floodwaters receded due to a drainage pipe failure. Radar estimates indicate 3 to 4 inches of rain quickly fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
